title: [R3-8 successor] Carry the finalizer's attemptVersions into the release fence instead of re-reading them
description:
FILED BY architect-fdbab575 2026-08-28 while re-planning task-06835dfad0aa4ecd9801d760fc559ee8 (R3-8) on the governor's 16:28Z mandate. This row carries the half of R3-8's DoD 3 that could not fit inside the ten-file cap, and it closes the RESIDUAL WINDOW that R3-8 deliberately leaves open and states.

WHAT R3-8 CLOSES: the release commit becomes ONE `commitExpectedVersionDecisionLegs` decision whose seven read-only fence legs carry the versions at which the resource, activation, dispatch, step, journal, provider-run and release-handoff-binding aggregates were read AT THE RELEASE SEAM. That closes the window the PR #3 reviewer named: "change a source after the final read but before commit".

WHAT REMAINS, AND IS THIS ROW: `attempt-finalization-service.ts` ~:107-116 measures `attemptVersions` (activation + dispatch counts, via attempt-finalization-sources.ts ~:44-49), USES them for its terminality decision, and DISCARDS them. R3-8 then RE-READS those two aggregates at the release seam. So the interval between the finalizer's read and the release read is unfenced: an aggregate can move there, the finalizer's terminality decision is then based on stale state, and the release records daemon-verified evidence derived from it while every fence passes. Same defect class as R3-8, one layer up.

THE FIX SHAPE: thread the finalizer's measured `{aggregateId, version}` envelope through to the release writer and fence at THOSE versions rather than re-reading. Compose R3-8's landed fence-legs composer (apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-fence-legs.ts) — do NOT build a second one; that module deliberately takes no store and performs no read, so it already accepts carried versions and refuses a caller-supplied roster.

WHY IT IS A SEPARATE ROW AND NOT AN R3-8 AMENDMENT: including attempt-finalization-service.ts and its suite makes ELEVEN owned paths against the ten-file cap. Epic rail 8(A) directs splitting at planning time, and the governor invited it in the same handoff. This is not a narrowed DoD; R3-8's own completion record is required to state this residual explicitly.

MEASURED at HEAD ee36952e, stale by default — re-measure at claim: attempt-finalization-service.ts is 146 lines and porcelain-clean; `attemptVersions` at ~:107-116; sources at attempt-finalization-sources.ts ~:44-49. The four finalization outcomes (NO_OP, DRAINING, RELEASED, BINDING_WRITTEN_RELEASE_REFUSED) must stay distinct across this change.

R3-8's fence-legs composer is COMPOSED, not duplicated: `apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-fence-legs.ts` is imported and its exact-key input refusal is relied on. No second composer, no second authority API, no store change — `git diff --exit-code -- packages/store/` must be EMPTY at delivery, and the leg budget stays at 1 primary + 7 fences = 8 = MAX_DECISION_LEGS.

THE WINDOW ARM THIS ROW EXISTS FOR: interpose a REAL production write to the activation or dispatch aggregate BETWEEN the finalizer's measurement and the release commit — a window R3-8's fence cannot see because R3-8 re-reads after it. The commit must refuse with the exact fence code naming that aggregate, with ZERO release events. Hook the COMMIT CALL, never a read: R3-8's measurement records that a read-shaped interposer in the obvious position never fires and passes vacuously. DRILL: revert to re-reading at the release seam and this arm must go RED; a GREEN drill is a FINDING, never a pass to bank.

The four finalization outcomes stay distinct and re-asserted against the carried-version shape: NO_OP, DRAINING, RELEASED, BINDING_WRITTEN_RELEASE_REFUSED. A replay still answers NO_OP adding zero events and zero fences. Restores proven by `git diff --exit-code` for tracked paths plus SHA256 against a %TEMP% backup in a call separate from the restore.

A bare `pnpm test` covers no apps/** and is not evidence. Repo-wide red path-attributed merge-base versus HEAD with an EMPTY owned-path intersection; production files at or under 400 lines; explicit-pathspec commit of the owned paths only; the completion comment states that this row closes the finalizer-read-to-commit window and names task-06835dfa as the row that closed the final-read-to-commit window.

Landing it first would mean building a second composer, which taskRail 3 forbids.

OWNED PATHS: apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-finalization-service.ts and attempt-finalization-service.test.ts, plus the minimum threading edit at the release seam. Do NOT re-open attempt-release-fence-legs.ts to add a reading path: it takes no store and performs no read BY DESIGN, and a composer that could read could fence at a version nobody observed.

Fence legs carry VERSIONS ONLY. Nothing in this row re-derives terminality, the safe boundary, or the handoff; release-terminal-evidence.ts forbids a second definition. Read once, fence at that version.

Never soften the claim: the finding is closed only by a commit that cannot succeed if a fenced aggregate moved after the version it carries was READ. A tighter recheck, a shorter window or a retry is not closure.

Put the task id in the describe title of every new arm, and hook interposers on the COMMIT CALL rather than on a read — a read-shaped hook in the obvious position never fires and its arm passes vacuously (measured on R3-8).

Fail closed with exact code and layer; TDD; target <=250 lines per production source and split before 400; explicit-pathspec commits only, never `git add -A` and never a bare `git commit` — foreign WIP is live under apps/daemon/src/work.

implementationPlan.description:
WIDEN THE MEASUREMENT INTO A CARRIABLE ENVELOPE — apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-finalization-sources.ts.

THE CRUX, and the reason this row is not a two-line change: `attemptVersions` at :44 returns `string | null` — a CONCATENATED COMPARISON TOKEN, `` `${activationLen}:${dispatchLen}` `` built from two `readEvents().length` calls. It exists only to be `!==`-compared at service.ts:114 and then thrown away. A concatenated string cannot be carried into a fence: `composeAttemptReleaseFenceLegs` needs per-aggregate `{ aggregateId, slot, version }`, and the token has fused the two numbers past recovery.

Return the PAIR instead — the two observations, each with its aggregate id, its slot (`ACTIVATION` for `bound.aggregateId`, `DISPATCH` for `bound.target`) and its numeric version. Shape them so they drop straight into `AttemptReleaseFenceObservation` (attempt-release-fence-legs.ts:88-93) with no adapter: that interface is ALREADY exactly `{ aggregateId, slot, version }`, and ACTIVATION and DISPATCH are ALREADY members of the frozen `ATTEMPT_RELEASE_FENCE_SLOTS` roster. This row composes the landed contract; it does not invent a parallel one.

KEEP `null` MEANING WHAT IT MEANS. The current `catch { return null; }` distinguishes an unreadable store from a readable one. Preserve that: an unreadable head must stay distinguishable from a readable head at version 0, because the landed composer answers `unreadableFenceHead()` for exactly that case and fabricating a 0 would turn an unreadable stream into a silently passing fence. `null` is not zero — attempt-release-store.ts:235 already says so in its own comment.

RAIL 8(A): the return-type change reaches the two callers in attempt-finalization-service.ts and nothing else (step 1(e)). The typecheck is the oracle — if a third file reds, STOP and report rather than taking the path.

Assert it by driving a case where the two DIFFER — move the aggregate between the finalizer's read and the commit, then assert the composed leg carries the EARLIER number. If both reads would return the same value the assertion is unfalsifiable and proves nothing; constructing the divergence IS the test.
(4) Assert the sweep actually generated its cases; a zero-case sweep passes vacuously.
